subject: Requirements for /yx-ypm in the three dimensions no prior corpus covered: operator experience and diagnostics, governance and policy enforcement, performance and scale
rationale: Ruling Q-GLPNETO19-01: narrow the run to the THREE requirement dimensions that neither gavriella's /bk-3rtask 20260901T114835Z-889f (25 sources over polyglot-PM design, version resolution, supply chain/SBOM/PURL, diamond/lockfile/formal models) nor my own drafted corpus would surface. Disjointness here is by DIMENSION and by source kind, and is additionally disjoint from the prior run's 25 sources by construction: none of the three slices below reads package-manager reference documentation, resolver algorithm papers, or SBOM/provenance standards - those are already covered and are explicitly out of scope for every slice.
prior_run_excluded: 20260901T114835Z-889f (gavriella) - all 25 of its sources are out of scope for every slice below

slices.lens: What makes a package manager usable or unusable in practice, and what must a refusal say? Extract requirements for CLI design, error-message quality, and the diagnostic surface.
sources: PubGrub error-reporting design write-ups and the 'why did this fail' explanation problem
Cargo/npm/pip error-message redesign discussions and issue threads
CLI design guidelines (Command Line Interface Guidelines, GNU/POSIX conventions) as applied to package tooling
Developer-experience research on build-tool adoption and abandonment
Post-mortems where an unexplained dependency refusal led to --force / --legacy-peer-deps escape hatches
Diagnostic and error-taxonomy design (actionable vs descriptive errors)
excluded: package-manager reference documentation (covered by that run's slice A)
anything belonging to slices U2 or U3

slices.lens: How is a dependency convention actually enforced across many teams, and what makes it hold or rot? Extract requirements for policy expression, enforcement points, exceptions and organisational adoption.
sources: Policy-as-code engines applied to dependencies (OPA/Rego, Conftest) and admission-control patterns
Monorepo dependency governance at scale (Google/Meta/Microsoft engineering practice write-ups)
Allowlist/denylist, licence-policy and approval-workflow practice for third-party components
Exception and waiver management: time-boxed exemptions, expiry, re-review
Inner-source and platform-team adoption literature: why conventions fail when only some teams hold them
Change-management and deprecation-policy practice for shared internal libraries
excluded: package-manager reference documentation and resolver papers
anything belonging to slices U1 or U3

slices.lens: What breaks when the dependency graph gets big, and what must the tool guarantee about time and space? Extract requirements for graph scale, caching, incrementality and query performance.
sources: Build-cache and remote-execution design (content-addressed caches, cache-hit-rate engineering)
Incremental and query-based build architecture (Buck2/Bazel query engines, Salsa-style demand-driven computation)
Reported scale limits: resolution time, lockfile size, graph node counts in large monorepos
Registry and mirror performance, cold-start and offline-install behaviour
Storage/dedup strategies for package caches (pnpm content-addressable store, Nix store)
Observability of build and resolve performance
excluded: resolver correctness/algorithm papers (its slice B/D) - only PERFORMANCE reports are in scope here
anything belonging to slices U1 or U2
